gold.summary: A historical policy edit keeps invalidating implementer selections made after that edit.

findings.title: Removed sticky implementers become eligible again after restart
findings.detail: Sticky-target removal depends on changedCells, which exists only in memory. After an operator reset and daemon restart, startup applies the unchanged base policy, leaving changedCells empty. A resumed run's persisted implementer is then appended and pinned even though the effective cell excludes it. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { Store } from "./src/db/store.ts"; import { ProviderTracker } from "./src/router/providers.ts"; import { Router } from "./src/router/router.ts"; import { DEFAULT_POLICY, PROVIDERS } from "./src/router/catalog.ts"; const s = new Store(":memory:"); const t = new ProviderTracker(PROVIDERS, s, {}, {}); const base =
findings.failure_scenario: A run has persisted claude/opus from an operator cell. The operator resets that cell to codex/sol while the run is paused, then restarts the daemon before its next implement round. The resumed run invokes claude/opus instead of codex/sol.

gold.summary: A pinned candidate slot deadline exits without recording the chain-exhaustion question.

findings.title: Pinned verify chain drops the environment-retry exclusion and logs a misleading warning
findings.detail: For role verify in chain mode, `excludeModels` is cleared. But in engine.ts:1553 verify's `excludeModels` doesn't hold the implementer. It holds the previous verifier (`firstModel`), excluded so the environment-blocked retry runs on a different verifier. With a chain like verify=[A,B], the retry can run on A again instead of moving to B. When it does, the warning at line 632-373 says "verify used the implementer's vendor/checkpoint ... because this run pinned it", which is false: A is the earlier verifier, not the implementer.
findings.failure_scenario: Run with models.verify=["a/m","b/m"], where the first verification ends environment-blocked. The retry routes to a/m again, and the event log claims a/m was the implementer's vendor/checkpoint.

findings.title: A single-model review chain can't verify panel findings when production review runs in panel mode
findings.detail: With a review chain, the panel verifier is routed through the chain, but `verifierConstraints` still hard-excludes (`excludeModels`) every model that raised a candidate. If the operator configures production review as a panel and pins review=[X], every finder runs on X. Any raised finding then has no eligible verifier, so the run goes to needs_human, even though the operator asked for X on review.
findings.failure_scenario: Config sets the production review system to panel mode; run created with models.review=["claude/opus"]. A finder raises a finding, the verifier has no candidates, and the run goes to needs_human.

gold.summary: A fixed review-time cutoff excludes worktrees created before the sidecar-writing release actually started.

findings.title: Commit timestamp excludes legitimate pre-upgrade worktrees
findings.detail: A commit timestamp does not establish when an installation upgraded. An old release can create worktrees after this cutoff, leaving them without sidecars, but this migration excludes them. Resume then skips registration and fails with Missing trusted Git paths. Reproduction: `bun /private/tmp/lr-qaLO3W/claude-501/review-migration.ts`. Output: `{ worktree_provenance: null }`, followed by `AssertionError: Old-release worktree must be resumable` and `null !== 'legacy'`.
findings.failure_scenario: An installation still running the previous release completes prepare at 1791100001000, after the hardcoded cutoff, then upgrades with that run parked and its worktree missing a sidecar.

findings.title: Legacy local worktrees are registered against the wrong repository
findings.detail: The code always supplies cachePath, but supported older local worktrees remain attached to the source repository. Their factory cache may not exist, or may contain no matching worktree. Additionally, registration requires a bare owner, so supplying the source's .git alone cannot fix this. Reproduction: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-qaLO3W/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-qaLO3W/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-qaLO3W/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-qaLO3W/claude-501/review-local.ts`. Output: `error: Unsafe worktree Git administration`, caused by `ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat '.../repos/local-repo.git'`.
findings.failure_scenario: A legacy-eligible local run resumes with an intact linked worktree attached to repo.localPath and no sidecar. Registration inspects the unrelated factory cache and the run fails before resuming.

gold.summary: A definitively refused CI rerun remains pending indefinitely.
Passing security-test output incorrectly prevents a transient CI rerun.

findings.title: A classification error in one PR stops observation of every later PR in the same repository
findings.detail: `record` awaits `classifyCi` without catching its errors. `classifyCi` throws in many deliberately 'retryable' situations: any non-200 REST read (logs 404/410, access errors), zod parse failures, and the various 'Incomplete …' or 'Ambiguous …' checks. The error propagates out of the `for (const [i, pr] of known.entries())` loop in `observe`, so the PRs after this one are never recorded in that cycle. Because `ciPending` was already saved as true, the same PR throws again on every poll. A persistent condition such as expired job logs (410) therefore stops merge, close, CI and review detection for every later PR in that repository indefinitely. That in turn stalls reconcileMergedRuns and the l
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced with a test in $TMPDIR/rev/test/zz-review.test.ts. Setup: PR #1 has a timed-out Actions job whose logs endpoint returns 410, and PR #2 in the same repository is then merged. After 10 polls (`bun test test/zz-review.test.ts -t starves`) there are 0 `pr.merged` items, where 1 was expected.

findings.title: A rejected rerun request leaves the failure pending forever: no ci.needs_fix, and REST polling never stops
findings.detail: `claimCiRerun` sets outcome to 'rerun_requested' before the POST. If the POST returns anything other than 201, the code throws and the row stays 'rerun_requested', for example a 403 'job cannot be rerun', a 422, a workflow that has been disabled, or run retention having expired. On later polls the resolution loop finds `run_attempt <= origin.attempt` and continues. The classification loop then sees `prior.some(pending)` and continues, and `pendingRerun` makes classifyCi return false. The result: ci.needs_fix is never emitted, `ciPending` never clears, and every poll repeats the full REST inspection (main commit, check runs, run, PR checks). This contradicts the requirement to fetch REST only
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced with `bun test test/zz-review.test.ts -t rejected`: a timed-out job whose `POST actions/jobs/21/rerun` returns 403. After 10 polls the ledger outcome is ['rerun_requested'], there are 0 ci.needs_fix items, and 52 REST calls were made.

findings.title: The feed excerpt is the first 2000 characters of the raw job log, which is usually runner setup boilerplate
findings.detail: `emit(..., log || f.line)` quotes `excerpt.trim().slice(0, 2000)`. GitHub Actions logs begin with runner, image and checkout setup output, so for real failures the excerpt rarely contains the failing line. The signature line is extracted separately, but the excerpt adds little diagnostic value.
findings.failure_scenario: A typical Actions log with several KB of setup output before the failing test: the ci.needs_fix excerpt shows only the setup lines.

findings.title: The change is roughly twice the requested source budget
findings.detail: The request asked for about 250 changed source lines. The classifier alone is 399 lines, plus about 80 in the poller, two migrations (the second only alters a table the first created in the same change), and store helpers. Much of the size comes from defensive cross-validation (completion timestamps, sibling ambiguity, annotation counts), which also creates many of the throw paths behind the blocker above.
findings.failure_scenario: Not applicable (maintainability).

gold.summary: Rate-limit refusals leave rerun claims unresolved across cooldowns and restarts.
ANSI-colored Bun failures and pytest security failures are missed by the retry exclusion.

findings.title: Rate-limited rerun requests remain pending forever
findings.detail: HTTP 429 leaves the persisted claim as rerun_requested. Since GitHub rejected the request, run_attempt never advances. Subsequent inspections skip resolution and suppress both another request and ci.needs_fix. The added tests assume a later rerun appears despite the rejection, masking this case. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts". Output: "Initial inspection: Error: CI job rerun was not confirmed"; three subsequent inspections returned false; {"posts":1,"outcome":"rerun_requested","needsFix":0}; assertion failed: "Rejected rate-limited rerun remains pending forever; no retry or needs_fix".
findings.failure_scenario: A timed-out job qualifies for rerun, but its POST receives HTTP 429. After cooldown, GitHub still reports the original workflow attempt. Every subsequent poll retains the pending claim, including after restart.

gold.summary: Effort removal is persisted without checking policy cells hidden by operator overrides.

findings.title: A stored runtime model that collides with a config model, or whose provider is gone, stops the daemon from starting
findings.detail:
The Factory constructor loads `store.runtimeModels()` and throws `catalog collision: ` if a code or config model has the same id. It throws `unknown provider

` if the provider is no longer defined. Both are uncaught at boot. Making a runtime experiment permanent in config.toml under the same id is the natural next step, and that makes the next restart fail. `catalog remove` needs the running daemon, so the only way to recover is to edit the SQLite file by hand.
findings.failure_scenario: 1. Run `limitless catalog add omlx/new-local ...`. 2. Add `[[providers.models]] id = "new-local"` under the omlx provider in config.toml. 3. Restart. `new Factory` throws `catalog collision: omlx/new-local` and the daemon never starts.

findings.title: DELETE checks only operator routing cells, not the eval policy overlay
findings.detail: `remove` scans only `store.routingCells()`. A policy overlay loaded from `policyPath` (evals) that names a runtime model can be left pointing at a deleted id. The router would then skip it as a resolve error rather than refusing the delete.
findings.failure_scenario: An evals policy file names `omlx/exp`, a runtime model. `catalog remove omlx/exp` succeeds, and the live policy now names a missing model.

findings.title: Every health probe publishes provider status even when nothing changed
findings.detail: `checkHealth` now calls `this.publish` on every probe, success or failure, in addition to any publish from `setHealthy`. This adds SSE traffic every probe interval for each discoverable provider.
findings.failure_scenario: An idle system sends a provider SSE update every probe interval for each discoverable provider.

findings.title: Over the source-line budget
findings.detail: There are about 494 changed source lines against the requested budget of about 350. Part of this is smoke refactoring that goes beyond the requested catalog check: provider lookups that used to throw now `continue`, and enabled-provider filtering was added.
findings.failure_scenario: Not applicable. This is about the size of the change.

gold.summary: Retrying an unchanged run converts inherited model chains into explicit overrides.
Routing previews remain stale after quota or cooldown expiry without an event.
Clearing a default effort omits the field from PATCH and leaves the old value stored.
Catalog history disappears on reload and does not include changes made by another client.

findings.title: Clearing the default effort silently retains its previous value
findings.detail: When the effort input is emptied, the PATCH payload omits effort. RuntimeCatalog.patch merges omitted fields from the existing model, so Save succeeds while retaining the old default. Removing that effort from supportedEfforts also causes validation to fail against the retained default.
findings.failure_scenario: Edit a runtime model with effort high, clear Default effort, and save. Reopening the editor still shows high, and routing continues using it.

findings.title: Catalog history is limited to the mounted page
findings.detail: Catalog changes are recorded only in the local session signal after this page's mutations. Navigating away or reloading erases them, and catalog SSE updates never populate history. This does not provide the requested recent catalog change history.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a runtime model, navigate away, and reopen Setup. Its catalog history is empty. Changes made by another operator are also absent.

gold.summary: Embedded short registered secrets remain visible in digest fields.
MCP status returns private land reasons unchanged on direct and proxy backends.

findings.title: Digest lines have no length cap, so one long question or title can flood session context
findings.detail: Each row prints the full quoted title and summary; for questions, the summary is replaced with the full open question text. JSON quoting keeps a row on one line, so the 20-line limit holds. But nothing limits how long a row is. Output from a SessionStart hook goes into the agent's context, so a multi-kilobyte question or a long PR title (untrusted text) produces a very large digest.
findings.failure_scenario: A run asks a 5 KB clarification question. Every new session's digest injects all 5 KB into the context.

findings.title: Digest makes one or two HTTP calls per distinct run with no limit
findings.detail: For every distinct run in the candidate groups, the digest fetches `/api/runs/:id`, and also `/api/land?run=` when the run has a PR. Those calls happen one after another. The hook's `claude` consumer is never acknowledged by the digest itself and may not match the consumer the agent acks with. In that case the cursor stays at 0, the whole retained feed is rescanned at every session start, and the number of calls grows with the history.
findings.failure_scenario: An install with several hundred runs that have PRs never acks the `claude` consumer. Each SessionStart makes hundreds of sequential requests and may approach the hook timeout.

findings.title: Approval row is read twice in getRunDetail
findings.detail: `approvalFor` already runs `SELECT ... FROM review_approvals WHERE pr_url = ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1`. The new code runs the same query again only to get `created_at`. The source change is also about 380 lines against a budget of about 200.
findings.failure_scenario: There is no functional failure; this is a duplicate query and extra code.

gold.summary: Unicode and URL encodings evade privacy protection in status and digest fields.

findings.title: Honor the run's confirmed merged flag
findings.detail: The status schema drops run.merged, and the merged-state check never considers it. Existing delivery and reconciliation paths set merged=true without setting resolution.kind or creating a land entry. Consequently, status reports an already merged PR as unknown or needing review. Regression output: Expected "Landed"; Received "PR state unknown".
findings.failure_scenario: A succeeded run merges through the existing automatic delivery path, with run.merged=true, resolution=null, no land entry, and no poller snapshot.

findings.title: Include renewed review work triggered by unread PR activity
findings.detail: Review candidates are selected exclusively from PR-opened, round-delivered, and approval events. After those events are acknowledged, unread PR activity never reaches the current-state reconciliation, even when the approval is now stale. The real-Store regression produced Expected "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 1; Blocked lands: 0"; Received "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0".
findings.failure_scenario: A consumer acknowledges an approved PR's feed items. An external push changes its head, invalidates approval, and produces an unread pr.ci_passed event. The next session digest reports no review work.

findings.title: Exclude active review rounds from review attention counts
findings.detail: The digest checks approval and land state but ignores review.rounds. A PR remains listed as awaiting review while its requested changes are queued or running, although another changes verdict would be refused as already in flight. Regression output: Expected "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0"; Received "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 1; Blocked lands: 0".
findings.failure_scenario: The original PR-opened event remains unread and a changes verdict creates a queued review round. Running digest immediately lists the PR as requiring another review.

gold.summary: Digest title truncation occurs before filtering and discloses private prefixes.

findings.title: Unrequested change to the publication gate now blocks on deep encoding even with an empty denylist
findings.detail: `privateMatches` now repeatedly decodes `%xx` and literal `\uXXXX` escapes. After 5 rounds it returns a synthetic entry 0, and that entry is returned even when `private-strings.txt` is empty. `audit.ts` (every added diff line) and `repos.ts` (blob scanning) both consume this, so an MCP/digest feature now changes when publication is blocked for every run. This is outside the scope of the request (MCP tools and digest) and roughly doubles the size of the diff in security-sensitive code.
findings.failure_scenario: [redacted diagnostic]

findings.title: Short registered credentials cause substring withholding of whole MCP output fields
findings.detail: `loadOutputPrivacy` passes every registered credential to `privateMatches`, which does a case-insensitive substring match. `redactCredentials` deliberately skips substring redaction for secrets under 8 characters to avoid false positives. The new path bypasses that guard and replaces the entire field with `[withheld: private text]`. Because `createMcpServer` now applies this to the output of every tool (including keys), existing tools such as get_run and feed are affected as well as the new ones.
findings.failure_scenario: A config secret with a short value (e.g. 'run' or '1234') is registered. Every MCP response string containing that substring, such as run IDs or statuses, comes back as `[withheld: private text]`. I confirmed `privateMatches('run-123 status running', [{value:'run',entry:0}])` matches.

findings.title: Digest makes up to two sequential HTTP requests per distinct run in the SessionStart hook
findings.detail: After paging the whole feed since the cursor, the digest fetches `/api/runs/:id` and `/api/land?run=` sequentially for every distinct run across all three groups. A consumer that has never acknowledged (the default `claude` consumer in the suggested hook) scans the whole retained feed. That can mean hundreds of serial requests before the session starts.
findings.failure_scenario: A fresh consumer with 300 retained feed items across 150 runs makes about 300 serial requests every time a Claude Code session starts.

findings.title: GET /api/land?run=<unknown> throws a generic Error and likely returns 500 instead of 404
findings.detail: `list(runId)` throws `new Error("run not found")`. The HTTP handler has no mapping for it, unlike the other run routes, which return `error("run not found", 404)`.
findings.failure_scenario: `curl /api/land?run=nope` responds with a server error rather than 404.

findings.title: limitless_status gives no state or next action when the privacy policy cannot be read
findings.detail: When `loadOutputPrivacy()` returns null, `explainStatus` returns only `{land, openQuestions}` and drops `state` and `nextAction`. Those are generated, constant strings that contain no untrusted text, so the tool loses its purpose for no privacy benefit.
findings.failure_scenario: `private-strings.txt` is unreadable, so `limitless_status` returns `{land:null, openQuestions:0}` and the agent gets no guidance.

gold.summary: Smoke invocations do not honor the configured model-origin exclusions.

findings.title: Filter excluded verifiers before selecting a panel target
findings.detail: The exclusion check runs after the production panel selects one verifier. In src/pipeline/engine.ts:1336–1342, every configured verifier enters pickVerifier, and the chosen target is offered alone through `only`. An excluded first verifier therefore causes NoCapacityError even when a later allowed verifier is available. A focused Bun probe using the existing pickVerifier function and real Router returned `selected: openrouter/deepseek-v4-pro`, an empty selectedRoute with `origin excluded (CN; baseOrigin=CN)`, and a nonempty allowedRoute for codex/sol.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure exclude_origins=["CN"] and a production panel with verifier.targets=["openrouter/deepseek-v4-pro","codex/sol"]. An Anthropic finder raises a finding, and Codex is available. The panel picks DeepSeek, routing rejects it, and verification fails instead of selecting Codex.

gold.summary: The isolated post-check status still inspects populated submodules with their own git directories, so a submodule that points at the land clone's admin directory runs a clean filter from the clone's configuration, which the request says never applies after the checks.

findings.title: Isolated dirty check still recurses into nested repos (gitlinks) and runs their PR-writable config
findings.detail: `git status` without `--ignore-submodules` recurses into every gitlink in the pinned tree. The child process runs in that nested work tree's own .git, so it uses that repository's config and info/attributes. The script only disables filter/hook keys it found in the private repo. GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS is passed on to the child, but the nested repo's own `filter.*.clean` (and similar keys) are not overridden. PR code that runs unconfined can write `sub/.git/config` and `sub/.git/info/attributes` during the checks, and the post-check status then runs that command. That is exactly the #402 threat this change is meant to close. The old in-clone status had the same recursion, so this predates the
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced: clone contains gitlink `sub` (an embedded repo). After the commit, write `f filter=x` to sub/.git/info/attributes and set `filter.x.clean = touch MARKER; cat` in sub's config, then touch sub/f. Running `git --no-pager -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false --git-dir=$iso --w

findings.title: Writing info/exclude assumes `git init` created info/ from templates
findings.detail: `printf '%s' "$exclude" > "$push_repo/info/exclude"` needs the info/ directory. That directory comes only from the init template; objects/info is always created, but info/ is not. If a user's global config sets `init.templateDir` to a directory without info/, or a packaged git has no template dir, the redirect fails and `set -e` stops every land with a raw bash error.
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced: `git -c init.templateDir=<empty dir> init --bare r` produces only HEAD, config, objects/{info,pack} and refs. The printf to r/info/exclude would then fail with 'No such file or directory'.

findings.title: The pager scenario runs without a terminal and never checks for `--no-pager`
findings.detail: The request asked for a pseudo-terminal or, failing that, an assertion that `GIT_PAGER`/`--no-pager` is used. The `checks:pager` scenario plants core.pager and pager.status but runs without a TTY, and git never starts a pager without one. So the scenario passes even if both `--no-pager` and the isolation are removed. Only the separate assertion that post-check calls use the private git dir would catch a regression.
findings.failure_scenario: Remove `--no-pager` from safe_git and keep isolation: checks:pager still passes, so the test does not cover the pager part.

gold.summary: Removing a built-in model leaves persisted routing overrides unable to load at startup.
A runtime model attached to a retired provider prevents factory construction.
Historical run references prevent unrelated catalog mutations.

findings.title: `limitless local` crashes on remote_host values that aren't valid URL hosts
findings.detail: `manageLocal` runs `new URL(`http://${host}:8080`)` without catching errors. `remote_host` is passed to ssh as a destination, and some valid ssh destinations are not valid URL hosts, such as a bare IPv6 address (`fe80::1`) or a value with a port (`box:22`). For these, `new URL` throws a TypeError and `local up`/`status`/`down` aborts with an uncaught error, even though the code before the change just built a string and let the probe fail quietly. I confirmed with bun: `new URL('http://box:22:8080')` and `new URL('http://fe80::1:8080')` both throw 'Invalid URL'.
findings.failure_scenario: config.toml has `[local] remote_host = "fe80::1"`; running `limitless local status` throws 'TypeError: Invalid URL' instead of printing a report.

findings.title: Link to the GUIDE's LAN provider example lands on the wrong section
findings.detail: OPERATIONS links to `GUIDE.md#providers-1`. GitHub numbers repeated heading anchors in order, so `#providers` is the first 'Providers' heading (`### Providers`, line 472, where the new LAN example sits) and `#providers-1` is the second (`## Providers`, line 1058). The second section is the general provider-config section, not the LAN example.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader clicks the link in OPERATIONS and lands on the generic provider section rather than the LAN example.

gold.summary: Retired identifiers and catalog or routing history can publish registered credentials.

findings.title: Old [local] config keys are ignored without a warning
findings.detail: main.ts now reads only `remote_host`, `remote_model_path` and `remote_llama_binary`. An existing config.toml that still uses the old machine-prefixed keys loses remote llama.cpp management with no message. `local up` / `status` just report oMLX, as if remote management were not configured. The warning can be generic and doesn't need to name the old keys, e.g. warn about any unrecognised `[local]` key.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator upgrades with the old `[local]` keys still in config.toml and runs `limitless local up`. Only oMLX is reported and the remote llama.cpp unit is never started, with no hint why.

findings.title: Invalid remote_host crashes `local` with a raw URL TypeError
findings.detail: `new URL(`http://${host}:8080`)` throws on a host the URL parser rejects, such as a value with a space or an IPv6 address without brackets. The command dies with an unexplained TypeError before reporting anything, oMLX included. An `ssh` destination that starts with `-` is also passed through as an ssh option. The config file is owner-controlled, so this is a robustness problem, not a security one.
findings.failure_scenario: With `remote_host = "my host"`, `limitless local status` throws `TypeError: Invalid URL` instead of printing the oMLX status.

findings.title: Retry and eval resume of records naming the removed id are refused, not resumed
findings.detail: The new test asserts that resuming an interrupted eval whose request names the retired model returns 400 "unknown model ID". `retryRun` similarly re-validates an inherited `run.models` chain strictly, so retrying a failed run pinned to the old id also throws. Live runs routing through chains with the old id work, and so does rendering. But the request says records written before the change should 'still render and resume'. For evals and retries, the old ids now require operator action instead of skipping the retired target as the router does.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval interrupted before the upgrade includes the machine-named model among its targets. `POST /api/evals/:id/resume` returns 400 and the remaining targets cannot resume.

findings.title: Scope larger than budget; catalog-edit validation semantics changed
findings.detail:
The source diff adds about 194 lines and removes 94, against a budget of about 120 changed lines (mostly deletions). It also changes behaviour beyond the rename:
- `remove()` no longer has its explicit operator-policy guard; `apply` enforces it instead, with a different error message.
- Terminal runs no longer block model deletion.
- Catalog POSTs now succeed despite references that were already invalid.
- Setup.tsx gains UI for unavailable references.

These changes support requirement 4, but the scoped re-validation in `apply` is hard to follow.
findings.failure_scenario: No crash. Reviewers and maintainers have to reason through nested `filterRetiredTargets` + `validatePolicy` calls to understand what a catalog edit refuses.

gold.summary: JSON escaping lets ordinary logged credentials evade literal gate-output redaction.
Line callbacks store pieces of multiline credentials in failure excerpts.

findings.title: Review prompt input redaction strips terminal escape sequences from the patch under review
findings.detail: `reviewPrompt` now starts with `input = redactGateData(input)`. That runs `redactGateOutput`, which calls `stripVTControlCharacters` on every string field, including `patch`, `prompt`, `stat` and `implementerReport`. Reviewers therefore see a cleaned-up version of the diff instead of the code as written. `implementPrompt` and `verifyPrompt` rewrite all of their inputs the same way. The request asked for redaction of gate output only.
findings.failure_scenario: I ran `redactGateData({patch: "+console.log('\u001b[8mhidden\u001b[0m')"})` with bun. The patch came back as `+console.log('hidden')`. A change that hides escape sequences in its source is shown to the reviewer without them.

findings.title: Out-of-scope API-wide rewrite changes every JSON response, every SSE message and every artifact download
findings.detail: `json()` and `sse()` now pass every payload through redactGateData. That JSON round-trip strips escape sequences from all strings and adds `confinementError` to any object with `ok` and `output`. The artifact endpoint goes further: it parses each artifact and serializes it again. Pretty-printed JSON artifacts such as `gates-N.json` and `baseline-gates.json` come back compacted, and non-JSON artifacts such as `diff.patch` and `report.md` come back with escape sequences removed. The request named runGates as the single redaction point and the deploy tails as the only other place to change. The HTTP layer was never in scope, and this pushes the change far past the ~30-line budget.
findings.failure_scenario: GET /api/runs/:id/artifacts/diff.patch on a patch that contains ESC bytes returns a different patch than the one stored, and GET on gates-1.json returns single-line JSON instead of the stored pretty-printed form.

findings.title: redactGateData is a lossy deep rewrite applied to RunState, the report and cache values
findings.detail: redactGateData round-trips its input through JSON, so `Date` values become strings, `Map`/`Set` become `{}` and `undefined` keys disappear. It is applied to the whole RunContext state in the constructor, to the full report input, and to cached check values (`context.ts:402`). It also adds `confinementError: launchFailure(output)` to any object that has `ok` and `output` keys, whether or not that object is a GateResult. These are silent changes in shape outside gate output, from what the request describes as a one-place fix.
findings.failure_scenario: I ran `redactGateData({ when: new Date(0), m: new Map([[1,2]]), ok: true, output: 'x' })`. It returned `{ when: '1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z', m: {}, ok: true, output: 'x', confinementError: false }`.

findings.title: New gate results always include `confinementError`, which goes against the removed compatibility comment
findings.detail: The old code added `confinementError` only when it was true. Its comment said this kept results readable by strict schemas and older releases. Now every result carries `confinementError: false`. The diff also changes `confinementFailed` so that an explicit false skips the backstop scan of the output. Older releases reading newer cached gate results could reject the extra field.
findings.failure_scenario: An older release reads a gate cache or state row written by this version and validates it with a strict schema that does not allow `confinementError: false`.

gold.summary: Lossy excerpt line framing prevents matching multiline credentials before storage.
Failure excerpt collection retains unbounded bytes on very long output lines.

findings.title: Account for escaped credential lengths at runner cuts
findings.detail: The overlap uses literal credential lengths, but redactCredentials now also recognizes longer JSON-escaped variants. When the runner cuts through an escaped variant, neither full variant matches, and dropping the shorter overlap leaves credential characters in the result. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { registerCredential, runProcess } from "./src/util/proc.ts"; import { redactGateStreams } from "./src/gates/output.ts"; const secret = "\n".repeat(80) + "SYNTHETIC-TOKEN-12345"; registerCredential("REVIEW_SYNTHETIC", secret); const raw = JSON.stringify(secret).slice(1,-1) + "\x1b[0m".repeat(15965); const res = await runProcess({cmd:[process.execPath,"-e","process.stdout.write(process.ar
findings.failure_scenario: A gate prints a registered multiline credential through JSON serialization followed by enough terminal formatting to cross the runner cap. Normalization removes the formatting, exposing a credential suffix that survives storage and model feedback.

findings.title: Restore a byte bound on retained diagnostics
findings.detail: Replacing the previous 8,000-character per-line cap with retention of whole lines makes excerpt buffering unbounded in bytes. Every subsequent line beyond the line limit also joins and redacts the entire retained buffer. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { FailureExcerpts } from "./src/gates/failures.ts"; const excerpts = new FailureExcerpts(); for (let i=0;i<39;i++) excerpts.observe("x".repeat(1_000_000)); console.log(JSON.stringify({retainedDiagnosticCharacters: excerpts.lines.reduce((n,s)=>n+s.length,0),lines:excerpts.lines.length})); excerpts.observe("(fail) assertion"); console.log(JSON.stringify({resultCharacters:excerpts.result().length}));' Output: {"retainedDiagnosticCharacters":
findings.failure_scenario: A noisy gate emits dozens of very large diagnostic lines. The daemon retains all their contents and repeatedly copies them during redaction, causing excessive memory use or termination.

gold.summary: An incomplete terminal escape consumes part of a credential before it can be matched.
Terminal-control stripping changes with chunk boundaries and loses state at the hold limit.

findings.title: Output privacy filter now withholds any text containing "[redacted]"
findings.detail: loadOutputPrivacy now returns "[withheld: private text]" for any string that contains the literal "[redacted]", even though redactCredentials has already made it safe. This filter covers MCP tool results and the digest. Because this change makes redacted gate output (and harness-redacted agent text) contain that marker, a whole gate diagnostic disappears from MCP and the digest once any registered credential appears in it. Text that merely mentions the word is also dropped. The request did not ask for this change (the MCP and digest paths are out of scope).
findings.failure_scenario: In a TMPDIR copy, a two-line script printed "[withheld: private text]" for both loadOutputPrivacy()("error: expected 1 got 2\napi key: [redacted]\nmore diagnostics") and loadOutputPrivacy()("docs: secrets are shown as [redacted] in logs"). MCP clients lose the whole gate failure output instead of se

findings.title: HTTP layer rewrites every API response and artifact (out of scope, alters data)
findings.detail: json() and sse() now send every payload through redactGateData. That strips VT control characters from every string, redacts it, and adds a `confinementError` field to any object with both `ok` and `output` keys. The artifact endpoint JSON-parses each artifact and re-serializes it, so artifacts written as pretty-printed JSON (gates-N.json, baseline-gates.json, etc.) come back compacted. Plain-text artifacts such as diff.patch lose any literal ESC sequences. The request asked for redaction once, where runGates builds a result, and does not mention HTTP serving.
findings.failure_scenario: In a TMPDIR copy, redactGateData(JSON.parse(prettyArtifact)) returned compact JSON with an added confinementError:false. A diff string containing "\u001b[31m" came back with the escape sequence removed, so GET /api/runs/:id/artifacts/diff.patch no longer serves the stored patch byte for byte.

findings.title: Blanket redactGateData over whole prompt inputs, run state and checkpoint caches
findings.detail: implementPrompt, reviewPrompt, verifyPrompt, renderReport, the RunContext constructor and every checkpoint cache hit now deep-clone their whole input through JSON and strip VT characters from every string (spec, user prompt, feedback, paths). The request was to redact once at the source so that every consumer receives redacted text. This defensive layering is large, easy to forget, and blurs where the boundary really is. It is a big part of why the change is ~300 source lines against a ~30-line budget.
findings.failure_scenario: A user prompt or spec that contains terminal escape characters is silently changed in every prompt and report. Every cache hit and RunContext construction also pays for a full JSON round trip.

findings.title: stdoutTruncated/stderrTruncated added but unused in source
findings.detail: The new ProcResult fields are only read by tests (hardening.test.ts). No source consumer uses them. This adds churn that the request did not ask for.
findings.failure_scenario: None at runtime. This is dead API surface.

gold.summary: Configuration errors and encoded feed diagnostics can disclose registered secrets.
A failure after configuration replacement leaves initialization partially applied.
Doctor omits health probes for implicit providers and presets lacking an explicit health URL.
The command fake permits mutating operations during read-only diagnosis.
The registration test does not exercise preservation of existing vendor settings.

findings.title: Apply newly written settings to an already healthy daemon
findings.detail: Service installation is skipped whenever the preflight daemon check passes, even after init changes config.toml. The daemon retains its startup Config and provider catalog, so newly detected providers and the selected merge policy remain inactive. The probe returned `{"probe":"healthy daemon and new repo","code":0,"installs":0,"repoReads":[],"providersAdded":["claude","codex"],"merge":"pr"}`. In particular, a daemon started with the default auto merge policy can continue auto-merging after init reports the safer pr policy.
findings.failure_scenario: Start a daemon with an empty config, then run init while its SHA matches. Init writes providers and github.merge="pr", reports success, and leaves the running daemon using its old settings.

findings.title: Check access to repositories supplied during init
findings.detail: Doctor runs before init collects repositories and only reads the first repository already in the saved config. Newly supplied --repo values or interactive answers are never checked for access or SSO before being persisted. The probe supplied private-org/blocked and returned code 0 with `"repoReads":[]`; its fake would record every gh API call. Thus the advertised repository preflight cannot diagnose organization access on a fresh installation.
findings.failure_scenario: On an empty config, gh auth status succeeds but the token lacks access to the organization supplied through --repo. Init writes that repository and proceeds without detecting the access failure.

findings.title: Run smoke checks against the configured provider catalog
findings.detail: The new adapter calls scripts/smoke.ts main(), which still builds checks from hard-coded PROVIDERS and MODELS. It ignores detected local providers and configured endpoint/model overrides, and always checks both native CLIs. The probe configured ["claude","codex","local-1234"], but smoke enumeration contained only Claude, Codex, omlx, twilight, OpenRouter and TypeSafe checks, with none for local-1234. This leaves the newly configured backend unverified and can fail setup for a CLI that doctor explicitly allowed to be absent.
findings.failure_scenario: Init detects a local server on port 1234 whose model listing succeeds but inference is broken. Its smoke phase never invokes that server, so setup can report success without validating the selected backend.

findings.title: Implement the requested discreet-mode setup choice
findings.detail: Discreet mode is represented only by a hard-coded skipped message. Init neither asks for the preference nor persists it, despite this being an explicit setup requirement. The interactive probe recorded only provider, repository, merge-policy and MCP questions; no discreet-mode question occurred.
findings.failure_scenario: A user runs interactive init intending to enable discreet mode for work repositories. Setup completes without offering or saving that choice.

gold.summary: LFS exemptions permit missing payloads and pointer replacements containing archives.
The limited text sample exempts a TAR whose first binary byte lies beyond the sample.
The WebP inspector rejects valid lossy VP8 images.

findings.title: Restore every explicitly requested inert media extension
findings.detail: INERT_MEDIA_PATH omits PDF, MP4, BMP, AVIF, TIFF, HEIC, PSD, EOT, several audio/video formats, and all requested 3D formats. These now require an allowance, contrary to the request. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-media.ts"` with the repository's complete PDF fixture produced a binary-content finding with severity block for document.pdf; allowed: []. The added tests explicitly expect PDFs to block, encoding the opposite acceptance criterion.
findings.failure_scenario: A request adds or edits an ordinary PDF or MP4 without Allow: binary; the audit blocks delivery.

findings.title: Do not classify incidental media bytes as executable payloads
findings.detail: clean rejects magic sequences anywhere in encoded or decoded media, including the two bytes MZ. Those bytes are valid PCM samples and can occur naturally in compressed images or audio. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-media.ts"` after replacing two sample bytes in the valid WAV fixture with MZ produced a binary-content finding with severity block for pcm.wav. The WAV structure remained unchanged.
findings.failure_scenario: An otherwise ordinary WAV contains adjacent sample bytes 0x4d, 0x5a and incorrectly requires Allow: binary.

findings.title: Preserve the exemption for PNGs with ordinary metadata
findings.detail: The PNG parser rejects every ancillary chunk outside its small allowlist, including standard tEXt, iTXt and iCCP chunks. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-media.ts"` with a valid CRC-protected tEXt chunk containing Title and Ordinary photo produced a binary-content finding with severity block for title.png, while the original clean.png passed. Ordinary image metadata was not excluded by the request.
findings.failure_scenario: A PNG exported with a title, copyright notice, or embedded color profile blocks without Allow: binary.

findings.title: Avoid imposing an unrequested decoded media size cutoff
findings.detail: The 32 MiB decompression cap removes the exemption from ordinary high-resolution images, even when their committed blobs are tiny. `bun "$TMPDIR/review-media-size.ts"` generated valid blank RGB PNGs and returned {"width":2048,"bytes":12300,"decoded":12584960,"inert":true} followed by {"width":4096,"bytes":48995,"decoded":50335744,"inert":false}. Thus a valid 49 KB PNG incorrectly requires an allowance.
findings.failure_scenario: Adding or editing a 4096×4096 RGB PNG without Allow: binary produces a blocking binary-content finding.

gold.summary: A bare executable magic match rejects valid image bytes with an incidental signature.

findings.title: Restore all required inert media exemptions
findings.detail: The exemption includes only five image types, omitting explicitly required fonts, audio, video, PDF, other images and 3D models. Running `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-check.ts"` with the supplied valid fixtures reported asset.pdf, asset.wav and asset.woff2 in binaryPaths for both additions and edits. New tests incorrectly require these formats to block.
findings.failure_scenario: A request without Allow: binary adds or edits a valid WOFF2 font, PDF document, or WAV asset; the audit blocks it.

findings.title: Do not classify arbitrary signature substrings as binary
findings.detail: isForbiddenFormat searches complete text blobs for short signatures and ordinary strings. The classification then removes matching files from the text set. Running `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-check.ts"` on ordinary.ts containing `const signature = "MZ";` produced a blocking binary-content finding, despite the file being fully readable text. Strings such as ustar and SQLite format 3 cause the same problem.
findings.failure_scenario: A normal source or documentation edit mentions MZ, ustar, or SQLite format 3 and unexpectedly requires Allow: binary.

findings.title: Preserve readable executable scripts without a binary allowance
findings.detail: modeRequiresAllowance is true for every changed file with mode 100755, regardless of content. Its unconditional inclusion in binaryPaths blocks readable shell scripts and executable text programs. Running `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-check.ts"` with a 0755 script.sh containing `#!/bin/sh\necho hello\n` produced a blocking binary-content finding.
findings.failure_scenario: A request adds or edits a readable executable shell script without Allow: binary; the audit rejects it even though Git displays its contents.

findings.title: Allow ordinary PNG metadata
findings.detail: The PNG parser rejects valid ancillary chunks outside its small whitelist, including ordinary tEXt metadata. Running `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-media.ts"` using the supplied PNG fixture and a correctly checksummed tEXt chunk containing Author/Test printed `plain PNG: true` and `valid PNG with tEXt Author metadata: false`. Consequently, ordinary PNG assets require an allowance contrary to the acceptance criteria.
findings.failure_scenario: A valid PNG exported with author, copyright, or software metadata is added or edited; isInertMedia rejects it and the audit blocks publication.

gold.summary: Shutdown drops an already claimed descendant when its parent exits.
Holdout snapshot deletion proceeds despite unconfirmed descendant termination.
Production scratch directories are never registered as process ownership roots.
Replacing a descendant environment removes it from invocation discovery.

findings.title: Children with replacement environments survive shutdown
findings.detail: Processes with readable environments are selected only by invocation markers. A background Bun child spawned with env:{PATH:process.env.PATH,FOO:'bar'} loses those markers and is ignored even in the invocation's process group. The Linux scanner likewise requires markers. Standalone command `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501/review-process-tree.ts` returned `{"exitCode":0,"childAliveAfterReturn":true}`. Cleanup can therefore begin while invocation descendants remain alive.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer starts a background writer using a sanitized environment and exits or stalls. The writer survives invocation shutdown and races worktree cleanup.

findings.title: Cwd and birth time incorrectly establish process ownership
findings.detail: Any hidden-environment orphan born after invocation start with a cwd under the worktree is treated as an invocation member, without evidence of ancestry. This kills unrelated processes sharing that directory. A standalone check launched an independent sibling launcher that orphaned a shell in the invocation cwd. Command `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501/review-unrelated-orphan.ts` returned `{"exitCode":0,"unrelatedOrphanAliveAfterReturn":false}`.
findings.failure_scenario: While an invocation runs, another worker or user starts a detached platform process in the same checkout. Invocation shutdown kills that unrelated process.

findings.title: Gate timeout rerun bypasses cleanup retry and recovery
findings.detail: The second checkoutCommitted call omits retryClean even when implementerIssue is set. If this clean fails, it throws CommandError rather than WorktreeCleanError, so the new recovery handler rethrows it and fails the run. A standalone probe of this call's default behavior, `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501/review-clean-retry.ts`, produced `{"errorType":"CommandError","cleanAttempts":1}` for a clean that would succeed on its second attempt.
findings.failure_scenario: A stuck implementer leaves partial work, gates time out only on the changed revision, and git clean fails once before the gate rerun. Even if final discard succeeds, the run fails instead of retrying cleanup or advancing rounds.

gold.summary: Run-wide scratch roots let one invocation cleanup kill another invocation writer.
A recycled leader PID claims unrelated processes through reused group or session identifiers.

findings.title: Working directory does not prove ownership of an orphan process
findings.detail: The orphan fallback selects any hidden process born during the invocation whose cwd is under a recorded directory, even without an invocation marker, matching session/group, or proven ancestry. stopMarkedProcesses then signals that unrelated process. A standalone probe launched an independent orphan and called discovery with an unrelated marker/group. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-process-probes.ts" orphan. Output: {"unrelatedProcessSelected":true}.
findings.failure_scenario: Another tool starts a background process in the checkout during an invocation and its launcher exits. On macOS, shutdown can classify that unrelated orphan as an invocation descendant and terminate it.

findings.title: Detached descendants can still write after shutdown reports success
findings.detail: Discovery begins during termination, so ancestry is already lost when a detached descendant has replaced its environment and its parent has exited. A cwd outside the recorded roots also bypasses the fallback. A real runProcess probe returned successfully while its descendant continued writing into the worktree by absolute path. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-process-probes.ts" escape. Output: {"exitCode":0,"writerAlive":true,"continuedWriting":true}. This escape predates the change but leaves the requested whole-tree shutdown guarantee unmet.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer launches a detached helper with a clean environment and a temporary cwd, then exits. The helper keeps writing to an absolute worktree path after runProcess resolves, allowing cleanup to race with the surviving writer.

gold.summary: The reader loopback policy cannot match the intended socket access.
An allow-default reader policy weakens the established confinement boundary.

findings.title: Disable the HTTP idle timeout for long verification commands
findings.detail: Bun.serve defaults to a 10-second connection idle timeout. This endpoint uses JSON responses and awaits the entire subprocess result before returning any bytes, so verification commands exceeding that interval lose their MCP connection even when the subprocess produces output. The request signal is included in the subprocess cancellation signal, so disconnecting can also terminate the test. Increasing the CLI tool timeout does not change this server timeout.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier invokes a test suite taking 20 seconds with timeoutMs set to 180000. The HTTP connection times out around 10 seconds before the command result is returned, causing a tool transport failure instead of successful verification.

gold.summary: A single extracted test command is treated as proof of a multi-step criterion.

findings.title: Do not treat one covered command as coverage of an entire scenario
findings.detail: The regex extracts a Bun command while ignoring additional instructions, then marks the entire blocked criterion met. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {applyGateEvidence as f} from "./src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts"; const sha="a".repeat(40); console.log(f({criteria:[{id:"A",status:"blocked"}]},{acceptance_criteria:[{id:"A",how_to_verify:"bun test a.test.ts\nCheck outbound access is denied"}]},{scenarios:[]},sha,{sha,stageId:1,checks:[{verdict:"pass",blocking:false,testCommand:"bun test",result:{ok:true,exitCode:0,output:"a.test.ts:\n(pass) loopback"}}]}).criteria[0].status);' Output: met. No gate evidence covers the outbound check.
findings.failure_scenario: A scenario requests a loopback test followed by an independent outbound-denial check. Gates cover only the loopback test; the verifier reports blocked on the other step. The factory changes the whole scenario to met and can deliver without verifying outbound isolation.

findings.title: Check tested working-tree bytes before recording commit provenance
findings.detail: Evidence eligibility checks only HEAD, after discardChanges has erased gate modifications. Setup commands and earlier checks can modify tracked source or tests without changing HEAD. Subsequent tests then pass against those modified bytes, but the new evidence attributes that pass to the original commit and can override a blocked independent verification.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured setup or fixing check rewrites a tracked source file so the loopback test passes. Gates succeed, discardChanges restores the broken committed file, and HEAD remains unchanged. When the reader cannot run the test, its blocked result becomes met using evidence from the repaired working tr

gold.summary: Matching a successful command does not establish the observation required by the criterion.
Targeted Bun evidence can satisfy a criterion without proof that any tests ran.

findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests prevent resolving the reported verification failure
findings.detail: Substitution requires every gate to contain zero skipped tests, even when coverage proves the requested file passed completely. This repository deliberately skips Seatbelt tests inside confined gates, so its normal full-suite gate cannot supply evidence for passing loopback tests. Since the reader profile remains unchanged, the original needs_human failure persists. Reproducer: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-383.ts" skips` outputs `expected met; actual blocked` and `AssertionError: 'blocked' !== 'met'`.
findings.failure_scenario: The full-suite gate passes test/loopback.test.ts and skips test/seatbelt.test.ts as required inside confinement. The verifier reports a sandbox block for the loopback test. Substitution refuses the passing evidence and verification ends as needs_human.

findings.title: Targeted-command shortcut certifies a file that never ran
findings.detail: The shortcut normalizes away './' and accepts matching command arguments without consulting passedFiles. Bun treats an unprefixed argument as a substring filter, while './' selects a path. With only other-loopback.test.ts present, `bun test loopback.test.ts` passes but `bun test ./loopback.test.ts` fails with no matches. The resolver nevertheless marks the latter criterion met, even with coverage explicitly naming only the unrelated file. Reproducer: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-383.ts" filter` outputs `gate exit=0; requested command exit=1`, `expected blocked; actual met`, and `AssertionError: 'met' !== 'blocked'`.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate runs the filter `bun test loopback.test.ts`, discovering only other-loopback.test.ts. A sandbox-blocked criterion requires `bun test ./loopback.test.ts`, whose file is absent. Verification incorrectly passes using the unrelated test.

gold.summary: An inherited Git configuration selector redirects trusted SSH lookup into the checkout.
Trusted remote-dependent credential and SSH settings no longer apply during push.
Manual landing publishes a fork branch to the upstream repository.
Forcing HTTPS during manual push bypasses working SSH authentication.

findings.title: Trusted URL-conditional credentials disappear
findings.detail: Replacing GIT_COMMON_DIR removes remote URLs used to evaluate trusted global includeIf.hasconfig:remote.*.url conditions. Consequently, credential helpers and SSH settings in those trusted includes disappear. A local probe with GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=0 confirmed that `git config --get credential.helper` returned `trusted-helper` before isolation, while `bash scripts/push-git.sh <capture> push https://example.invalid/repo.git HEAD:refs/heads/test` queried the same effective setting and returned exit 1 with empty output.
findings.failure_scenario: The global config selects a credential helper through a hasconfig remote-URL condition matching the checkout's origin. Ordinary pushes authenticate, but delivery and landing pushes lose that helper.

findings.title: The SSH default overrides trusted GIT_SSH
findings.detail: When core.sshCommand is unset, injecting core.sshCommand=ssh overrides Git's existing GIT_SSH environment setting. A network-free probe used GIT_SSH to run a local receive-pack: `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null push "$destination" "$sha:refs/heads/before"` succeeded, while `bash scripts/push-git.sh git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null push "$destination" "$sha:refs/heads/after"` exited 128 with `fatal: Could not read from remote repository.` The invocation markers were `trusted` followed by `fallback`, proving the wrapper bypassed GIT_SSH.
findings.failure_scenario: An installation supplies its SSH identity or authentication wrapper through GIT_SSH and has no global core.sshCommand. Factory pushes now invoke plain ssh and fail authentication.

findings.title: Hardcoded HTTPS breaks existing SSH authentication
findings.detail: The final push previously used origin's transport and now always uses HTTPS. An SSH-only installation with working global SSH configuration gains no HTTPS credentials from that change, so landing fails after checks and the final scan. This violates the requirement to preserve existing helper or SSH authentication.
findings.failure_scenario: The landing checkout has an SSH origin, authentication works through an SSH key, and no HTTPS credential helper or URL rewrite is configured. The final push switches to HTTPS and cannot authenticate.

gold.summary: The loop detector aborts before the threshold call can return evidence of progress.

findings.title: The sixth call aborts before its changed result can establish progress
findings.detail: observe() returns the stop reason before receiving the current result. Both harnesses immediately abort and retain stuckReason, so observeResult() cannot rescue the run. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); for(let i=0;i<5;i++){d.observe("shell","poll",String(i));d.observeResult(String(i),"waiting");} console.log(d.observe("shell","poll","5"));d.observeResult("5","progress");' Output: repeated the same shell call 6 times. The changed sixth result should restart the count.
findings.failure_scenario: Five identical polls return 'waiting'; the sixth poll returns 'progress'. The harness aborts at the sixth call before considering its changed result.

findings.title: Late results overwrite the baseline of newer identical calls
findings.detail: results stores the last completion rather than the previous identical call in invocation order. An older completion can replace a newer hash, causing the next unchanged result to clear the window incorrectly. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100);for(let i=1;i<=3;i++)d.observe("shell","poll",String(i));d.observeResult("1","A");d.observeResult("3","B");d.observeResult("2","A");for(let i=4;i<=9;i++){const r=d.observe("shell","poll",String(i));d.observeResult(String(i),"B");if(i===9)console.log(r);}' Output: null. Calls 4–9 repeat result B after call 3 established B, so the sixth repetition should stop.
findings.failure_scenario: Identical calls 1–3 produce A, A, B but complete in order 1, 3, 2. Calls 4–9 all produce B. Call 4 is incorrectly classified as progress, delaying loop detection.

gold.summary: Unresolved tool calls accumulate without a bound during a live invocation.

findings.title: Missing results can suppress loop detection entirely
findings.detail: Unresolved calls remain uncounted until finish(), block later completions of the same key, and can be evicted before ever counting. This violates the requirement that calls whose results never arrive retain today's counting. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); for (let i=0;i<6;i++) console.log(`missing ${i+1}:`, d.observe("shell", "poll", String(i))); for (let i=0;i<12;i++) d.observe("Read", {path:String(i)}, `read-${i}`); console.log("finish:", d.finish());'. Output: missing 1: null through missing 6: null, then finish: null. The previous detector stops at the sixth shell call. A separate direct check also sho
findings.failure_scenario: Six identical tool calls receive no results, then unrelated calls evict them from the window. The invocation ends without a loop verdict. Alternatively, an early unresolved call blocks later identical completed results until it leaves the window.

gold.summary: Increasing panel test deadlines leaves the underlying parallel Git race undiagnosed.
Factory gate environment construction discards the configured test worker override.

findings.title: Worker override is stripped before factory gates run
findings.detail: gateEnv() uses agentEnv(), which removes LIMITLESS_* variables. Consequently, this command always defaults to four workers in factory and land gates. Reproduction: LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS=2 bun -e 'import { gateEnv } from "./src/gates/run.ts"; console.log(gateEnv().LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS); if (gateEnv().LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS !== "2") throw new Error("worker override stripped")'. Output: undefined; error: worker override stripped. Evaluating the configured worker expression with gateEnv() likewise returned 4.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator sets LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS=2 to reduce contention between factory gates; each gate still starts four workers.

findings.title: Required benchmark evidence is missing
findings.detail: The change selects four workers but provides no implementation report containing the requested 4/6/8 comparison, serial versus parallel wall and CPU times, post-split top ten files, or three successful parallel suite runs. The targeted checks here cannot establish those acceptance criteria.
findings.failure_scenario: The change is accepted without evidence that the chosen default improves suite cost or that the split and timeout change run reliably under parallel load.

gold.summary: Unlimited quota still applies utilization reserves to free and metered providers.

findings.title: Honor unlimited quota independently of billing type
findings.detail: The config accepts unlimited quota for every billing type, but headroom ignores windows only for subscriptions. Free and metered providers still become unavailable at their reserve despite displaying “No limit (configured)”. Probe command: `bun --eval 'import { Store } from "./src/db/store.ts"; import { ProviderTracker } from "./src/router/providers.ts"; const store = new Store(":memory:"); const reserves = {claudeFiveHour:0.8,claudeSevenDay:0.85,codexFiveHour:0.9,codexWeekly:0.9}; for (const billing of ["subscription", "free", "metered"]) { const tracker = new ProviderTracker([{id:"work",label:"Work",harness:"claude",billing,quota:"unlimited",maxConcurrent:1}],store,reserves,{}, {}, () => 1
findings.failure_scenario: Configure a free or metered provider with quota="unlimited" and observe a 99% window. Routing incorrectly excludes it at the reserve limit.

findings.title: Clear persisted window alerts when switching to unlimited
findings.detail: Unlimited mode prevents new window alerts but leaves previously persisted alerts active until their reset, potentially indefinitely for a null reset. Probe command: `bun --eval 'import { Store } from "./src/db/store.ts"; import { ProviderTracker } from "./src/router/providers.ts"; const store = new Store(":memory:"); const reserves = {claudeFiveHour:0.8,claudeSevenDay:0.85,codexFiveHour:0.9,codexWeekly:0.9}; const def = {id:"claude",label:"Claude",harness:"claude",billing:"subscription",maxConcurrent:1}; const before = new ProviderTracker([def],store,reserves,{}, {}, () => 1000); before.observeWindows("claude",{seven_day:{utilization:0.99,resetsAt:604801000}}); const after = new ProviderTrac
findings.failure_scenario: A provider produces a seven-day quota alert, then the user configures unlimited mode and restarts. The old exhaustion alert remains visible despite the window becoming informational.

gold.summary: A pinned candidate slot deadline exits without recording the chain-exhaustion question.

findings.title: Keep previous implementers excluded after escalation
findings.detail: The tried-implementer exclusion applies only on the escalation round. Subsequent rounds pass only a preference for the current implementer, making earlier candidates eligible again. A temporary fake-harness regression run with `bun test /private/tmp/lr-JqGYnE/claude-501/chain-review-regression.test.ts --test-name-pattern 'review regression'` failed: `regression calls [ "alpha/m", "alpha/m", "beta/m", "beta/m", "alpha/m" ] status succeeded`. Expected calls ended after the second beta invocation, with needs_human. This violates the requirement to escalate to untried candidates and stop when the chain is exhausted.
findings.failure_scenario: Pin [A, B]. A produces failing changes for two rounds, so escalation selects B. B produces failing changes once, then reports quota exhaustion on its next round. Routing returns to A instead of stopping with needs_human.

gold.summary: Arbitrary assertion text mentioning a timeout is classified as a transient CI failure.
Retry eligibility ignores security failures outside the selected error line.
A paused PR is not inspected again when main recovers without another PR change.
An accepted rerun with a lost response is never reconciled to its later result.

findings.title: Reconcile reruns hidden beyond the GraphQL context limit
findings.detail: Outstanding reruns require ciChanged to trigger reconciliation, but the query retrieves only 100 contexts. A rerun outside that page can finish without changing ciKey when another check keeps the rollup red. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-B7dm2c/claude-501/ci-review-61z1i8mr/truncated-probe.ts`. The probe requested one rerun with ciPending=false, then completed it with timed_out beyond the first 100 contexts. After two polls, output showed newRestCalls=0, the target outcome remained rerunning, and ci.needs_fix existed only for the unrelated check.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR has over 100 check contexts. A transient failure outside the fetched page is rerun, while another check keeps aggregate CI red. The rerun fails again without changing any fetched context, so ci.needs_fix is never emitted.

findings.title: Compare repository identity without case sensitivity
findings.detail: The exact check_run_url comparison rejects valid jobs when GitHub's canonical owner/repository casing differs from the stored slug. Repository matching elsewhere explicitly supports casing differences. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-B7dm2c/claude-501/ci-review-61z1i8mr/probe.ts`. With stored slug o/r and job URL containing O/R, output was reruns=0, needsFix=0, pending=true, and `GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete failing job`. The second poll repeated the error and still requested no rerun.
findings.failure_scenario: A repository is configured with casing different from GitHub's canonical URL. Every failing Actions job is rejected, preventing reruns, ledger recording, and ci.needs_fix classification.

gold.summary: A definitively refused CI rerun remains pending indefinitely.
Passing security-test output incorrectly prevents a transient CI rerun.

findings.title: Resolve explicitly rejected rerun requests
findings.detail: The claim is persisted before POST, but an explicit rejection only throws. Subsequent inspections wait for a newer run attempt and suppress needs-fix reporting, although GitHub never accepted the rerun. Probe: `bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review-probe.test.ts"`. With POST returning HTTP 422, repeated polls printed `REJECTED {"outcome":"rerun_requested","needsFix":0,"pending":true,"reruns":1}`; the assertion expecting one needs-fix item failed with `Expected length: 1; Received length: 0`.
findings.failure_scenario: A timed-out job qualifies for rerun, but GitHub rejects the rerun POST with HTTP 422. No later attempt exists, leaving classification pending indefinitely.

findings.title: Isolate CI inspection failures to the affected PR
findings.detail: A classifyCi exception propagates through record() and aborts the repository's observation loop before later PR snapshots are saved. A persistently unavailable log therefore starves unrelated PRs on every poll. Probe: `bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review-probe.test.ts"`. With the first PR's log endpoint returning HTTP 404 and a second PR passing CI, repeated polls printed `NEXT_PR {"data":null,"errors":["GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: actions/jobs/21/logs (404)","GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: actions/jobs/21/logs (404)"]}`. The assertion requiring the second PR's snapshot failed with `Received: null`.
findings.failure_scenario: The first tracked PR has an unavailable or expired job log. Later PRs in the same repository stop receiving persisted CI, review, and merge observations until that endpoint recovers.

gold.summary: Catalog mutation can invalidate a shadowed retained policy and prevent the daemon from restarting.

findings.title: Make the escaped-process fixture independent of startup timing
findings.detail: Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun test test/smoke.test.ts --test-name-pattern 'smoke cleans CLI groups: escaped-timeout'. Observed repeatedly: Expected: 2; Received: 4. The fixture assumes readiness is observed before the 250ms timeout can trigger a retry, making the exact PID-count assertion timing-sensitive. A temporary baseline copy passed; the assertion and timeout logic are unchanged by this diff, so attribution to this change is not established.
findings.failure_scenario: The first attempt times out and a retry appends another PID pair before the test observes fixture readiness.

gold.summary: Retrying an unchanged run converts inherited model chains into explicit overrides.
Routing previews remain stale after quota or cooldown expiry without an event.
Clearing a default effort omits the field from PATCH and leaves the old value stored.
Catalog history disappears on reload and does not include changes made by another client.

findings.title: Catalog history omits changes received over SSE and disappears on reload
findings.detail: Catalog history reads only the local session signal, populated by this page's mutation callbacks. Catalog SSE refreshes never record changes, and remounting discards existing entries. This does not provide the requested recent catalog change history. Reproduction command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-catalog-history.ts". Output: "AssertionError: catalog deletion delivered over SSE should appear in recent change history", actual false, expected true.
findings.failure_scenario: Another operator deletes a runtime model. SSE removes it from the displayed catalog, but its deletion never appears in history. Reloading also removes locally recorded history.

findings.title: Clearing default effort silently preserves the saved value
findings.detail: An empty effort field is omitted from PATCH, but RuntimeCatalog.patch merges omitted fields from the existing model. Saving therefore retains the old default despite the cleared field. Reproduction command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-catalog-effort.ts". Output: "AssertionError: clearing default effort should unset the persisted default", actual "medium", expected undefined.
findings.failure_scenario: Edit a runtime model whose default effort is medium, clear Default effort, and save. The request succeeds but subsequent calls still use medium. Removing medium from supported efforts simultaneously instead causes validation failure.

gold.summary: Digest actions are derived from stale records instead of current unanswered and review state.
A historical failed review hides a later approval in MCP status.

findings.title: Exclude answered questions from the needs-you count
findings.detail: Answering a question produces no clearing feed event, so the digest continues requesting input while the run resumes. A store-backed reproduction using `bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-repro.ts"` printed `Open questions: 0` followed by `Needs you: 1; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0` and the answered question.
findings.failure_scenario: A question is emitted, answered without acknowledging the feed, and the run resumes. Every subsequent digest reports the answered question until a terminal clearing event occurs.

findings.title: Restore review attention when an approval becomes stale
findings.detail: The digest permanently removes a PR on review.approved, but an externally observed head change invalidates that approval without emitting either event that adds review candidates. The store-backed command `bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-repro.ts"` printed `Approval stale: true` followed by `Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0`. A fresh session therefore misses a PR requiring review.
findings.failure_scenario: A run opens a PR, its head is approved, and someone pushes another commit. The daemon observes the new head and marks the approval stale; digest still reports zero PRs awaiting review.

findings.title: Honor current approval after a failed review round
findings.detail: A historical failed or cancelled round takes precedence over the current PR approval. The review API permits approving a repaired PR after a round fails, but status continues directing the agent to inspect that round instead of landing. `bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-repro.ts"` returned `Status after approval of repaired PR: Review changes failed` for an open PR with a matching, non-stale approval.
findings.failure_scenario: A review round fails, a human repairs the branch, and the new head is reviewed and approved. With no land entry, limitless_status still reports the old round failure and never presents the next action to land.

gold.summary: Unicode and URL encodings evade privacy protection in status and digest fields.

findings.title: Honor the run's confirmed merged flag
findings.detail: The status schema strips run.merged, and the merged-state branch never checks it. Existing auto-merge delivery records merged=true without creating a land entry or requiring a saved PR observation. These successfully merged runs therefore report unknown state or request another review. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {explainStatus,statusDetailSchema as s} from "./src/integrations/mcp-status.ts"; console.log(explainStatus(s.parse({run:{id:"r",status:"succeeded",prUrl:"p",merged:true},questions:[]}),[]).state)' Output: PR state unknown.
findings.failure_scenario: An auto-merge run succeeds with merged=true, GitHub polling is disabled or has not updated, and no landing-queue entry exists.

findings.title: Exclude in-progress review rounds from awaiting-review items
findings.detail: The actionable predicate checks approval and land state but ignores review.rounds. After requesting changes, the original PR-opened event still causes the digest to request review of the old head while the factory is applying findings. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {digestCommand} from "./src/cli/digest.ts"; await digestCommand([],{}, {print:console.log,api:async p=>p.startsWith("/api/feed")?{items:[{id:1,kind:"run.pr_opened",runId:"r",data:{},title:"PR",summary:"p"}],nextAfter:1,pruned:false}:p.startsWith("/api/runs/")?{run:{id:"r",status:"succeeded",prUrl:"p"},questions:[],review:{approval:null,rounds:[{runId:"round",status:"queued"}]}}:[]})' Output includes: Needs you: 0; PRs await
findings.failure_scenario: A consumer has an unread PR-opened event, submits a changes verdict, then starts another session before the review round delivers.

findings.title: Format the new assertion so the required check passes
findings.detail: Command: bun run check. Output identifies test/mcp-proxy.test.ts:614 with 'Formatter would have printed the following content', followed by 'Found 1 error' and 'error: script "check" exited with code 1'. This newly added assertion prevents the required validation command from reaching typechecking and tests.
findings.failure_scenario: Running the required bun run check on this revision exits with status 1 during lint.

gold.summary: Layered URL and Unicode encodings bypass the single-pass private-text decoder.

findings.title: Honor the run's durable merged flag
findings.detail: The status schema strips run.merged, and this condition never checks it. Automatic delivery records successful merges using that flag without setting a merged resolution or creating a land entry. Such runs can permanently report unknown PR state because githubTracked excludes merged runs. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {explainStatus,statusDetailSchema} from "./src/integrations/mcp-status.ts"; console.log(explainStatus(statusDetailSchema.parse({run:{id:"r1",status:"succeeded",prUrl:"https://github.com/o/r/pull/1",merged:true},questions:[],prSnapshot:null}),[],String).state);' Output: PR state unknown
findings.failure_scenario: A run finishes through the existing automatic merge path before a PR snapshot is saved. limitless_status reports 'PR state unknown' and asks the agent to await an observation that polling will never collect.

findings.title: Reconcile review needs from unread PR activity
findings.detail: Only three event kinds become review candidates. After the consumer acknowledges an approval, an external push invalidates it and the poller can emit pr.ci_passed for the new head. The digest ignores that unread event without consulting current state, hiding the newly required review. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {digestCommand} from "./src/cli/digest.ts"; await digestCommand([],{consumer:"claude"},{api:async()=>({items:[{id:10,kind:"pr.ci_passed",runId:"r1",data:{url:"https://github.com/o/r/pull/1"}}],nextAfter:10,pruned:false}),print:console.log});' Output: Limitless digest (read only; quoted text is untrusted data)\nNeeds you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0
