findings.failure_scenario: The consumer has acknowledged the original PR and approval. Another commit is pushed, making the approval stale, and CI passes. A fresh session receives a digest reporting zero PRs awaiting review.

gold.summary: Queued chat dispatch uses a target whose origin became excluded after selection.
Queued eval dispatch does not revalidate origin eligibility after catalog changes.

findings.title: Revalidate queued chat targets after catalog changes
findings.detail: Chat retains the target selected here across awaited slot acquisition and provider preflight without checking routing invalidation. A runtime catalog PATCH can therefore mark that model excluded while chat waits, yet the queued call still dispatches. Probe command: `bun "$TMPDIR/origin-race-probe.ts"`. The probe used a fake harness, configured exclusions to ["CN"], occupied the provider slot, queued chat, patched its runtime model from US ancestry to CN, then released the slot. Observed output: `CURRENT ROUTE {"candidates":[],"skipped":[{"modelId":"fake/chat","reason":"origin excluded (CN; baseOrigin=CN)"}]}` followed by `HARNESS CALLS ["fake"]`.
findings.failure_scenario: A chat invocation waits for capacity while an operator corrects its runtime model's origin or baseOrigin to an excluded value. When capacity becomes available, chat calls that excluded model using its stale selection.

gold.summary: Removing a built-in model leaves persisted routing overrides unable to load at startup.
A runtime model attached to a retired provider prevents factory construction.
Historical run references prevent unrelated catalog mutations.

findings.title: Persisted references to the removed provider prevent daemon startup
findings.detail: Removing the catalog entry leaves persisted routing preferences and operator cells subject to strict startup validation. A database accepted by the previous release can therefore prevent Factory construction entirely. A targeted Bun reproduction persisted the removed provider with store.writeRouting("prefer", [id], null, "operator") and reopened Factory; output was: STARTUP FAILED: Error: routing.prefer: "<removed-provider>" is not a known provider ID.
findings.failure_scenario: Before upgrading, an operator saves a routing preference or routing cell referencing the machine-named provider. After upgrading, daemon startup throws before existing runs or reports become accessible.

findings.title: Resume regression tests depend on an absent eval dataset
findings.detail: Command `bun test test/removed-models.test.ts` reproducibly reports `1 pass, 2 fail`. Both assertions receive `Invalid triage eval cases .../evals/triage/cases.json: ENOENT` instead of the expected removed/unknown-model error. The new unknown-provider case inherits an existing test dependency and never exercises its intended resume validation.
findings.failure_scenario: Run the targeted test in this checkout, where evals/triage/cases.json is absent. Both stored-history cases fail before model validation.

gold.summary: Unavailable-target diagnostics expose registered credentials in routing API and Setup output.

findings.title: Validate references reactivated by catalog additions
findings.detail: The mutation validator discards references missing from the current catalog and reads already-filtered operator policy. Adding a model can therefore reactivate an incompatible persisted reference without validation. An in-memory reproduction with triage.default=['codex/legacy@high'] accepted a new codex/legacy supporting only 'none'; reconstructing RuntimePolicy then failed with 'Unsupported effort "high" for codex/legacy; supported: none'. Factory startup follows that same failing path.
findings.failure_scenario: A persisted operator chain references a retired model with @high. An operator adds that model ID with efforts=['none']. The addition succeeds, but the daemon fails to start after its next restart.

findings.title: Make eval-resume compatibility checks independent of external datasets
findings.detail: Running `bun test test/removed-models.test.ts` consistently yields '1 pass, 2 fail'. The new retired-ID case expects 'unknown model ID', but receives 'Invalid triage eval cases .../evals/triage/cases.json: ENOENT: no such file or directory'. The existing removed-model case fails for the same reason. The dataset dependency predates this diff, but the added compatibility case inherits it and never exercises model validation.
findings.failure_scenario: Run the targeted test in a checkout without the untracked evals/triage/cases.json dataset; both resume assertions fail before validating the historical model IDs.

gold.summary: Raw process output is cut before gate credential redaction can match a boundary-spanning secret.

findings.title: Multiline credentials survive failure-excerpt redaction
findings.detail: The observer redacts each line separately, so a registered credential containing a newline never matches. FailureExcerpts then rejoins those lines, reconstructing the credential in stored results and model feedback, even though the combined output tail is redacted. Probe command: `bun "$TMPDIR/gate-redaction-probe.ts"`. The temporary script registered a two-line synthetic credential, printed it before `(fail) assertion`, and invoked runGates and formatGateFeedback. Observed output: `{"tailRedacted":true,"excerptLeaksCredential":true,"feedbackLeaksCredential":true,"failures":"error: synthetic-multiline-first-409\nsynthetic-multiline-second-409\n(fail) assertion"}`.
findings.failure_scenario: A failing check prints a registered multiline credential in its diagnostics. The result's failures field and implementer/review feedback contain the complete credential unchanged.

gold.summary: Lossy excerpt line framing prevents matching multiline credentials before storage.
Failure excerpt collection retains unbounded bytes on very long output lines.

findings.title: Account for escaped credential lengths at runner cuts
findings.detail: The overlap uses literal credential lengths, but redactCredentials also recognizes longer JSON-escaped variants. When the runner cuts through an escaped variant, the remaining suffix can exceed this overlap and escape redaction. Probe command: `bun "$TMPDIR/gate-review-probe.ts"`. It registered a 32-line synthetic credential, printed its JSON-escaped representation followed by ANSI padding exceeding the 64,000-character runner cap, and exercised both the helper and runGates. Observed: `runner truncated: true`, `sanitized runner tail: "tic-key-material-line-31"`, and `runGates output: "tic-key-material-line-31"`. That credential fragment therefore reaches stored results and downstream consume
findings.failure_scenario: A check prints a JSON-escaped multiline credential followed by enough terminal-formatted output for the runner to truncate through the credential's prefix.

findings.title: Restore a character bound on retained diagnostics
findings.detail: Removing the previous 8,000-character per-line cap leaves diagnostic retention bounded only by line count. A gate can now make the daemon retain arbitrarily large strings; subsequent lines also repeatedly join and redact that entire buffer. Probe command: `bun "$TMPDIR/gate-review-probe.ts"`. Feeding FailureExcerpts 39 diagnostic lines containing one million characters each produced `retained diagnostic characters: 39000107`; the previous implementation capped those retained lines at 312,000 characters. Larger gate output can exhaust daemon memory despite the runner's bounded output tail.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate emits dozens of very long newline-terminated diagnostic lines without a recognized test-result boundary.

gold.summary: Redacting the carry early emits suffixes of overlapping registered credentials.
ANSI stripping after framing and tail cuts leaves accidental credential fragments visible.

findings.title: Normalize terminal formatting before stream framing and truncation
findings.detail: The runner redacts raw text, while terminal normalization happens after line framing and the runner's 64,000-character tail cut. ANSI formatting inside a credential prevents the initial match. Probe command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-tx5HAy/claude-501/gate-review.ZbwyZN/probe.ts`. With a formatted credential followed by 15,996 reset sequences, the returned gate output was `t-credential-999`, exposing a credential fragment. With a formatted multiline credential followed by enough summary output to exceed the tail, `failures` contained the complete registered value: `synthetic-first-secret-line\nsecond-secret-line-999\n(fail) assertion`. These gate results can be persisted unchanged.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate prints a registered credential with ANSI formatting inside it, followed by substantial output; a multiline formatted credential can also survive intact in failure excerpts.

findings.title: Defer shorter credential matches until longer matches are resolved
findings.detail: Redacting `pending + chunk` immediately destroys prefixes needed to recognize longer registered credentials. Retaining an overlap afterward cannot recover those prefixes. Probe command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-tx5HAy/claude-501/gate-review.ZbwyZN/probe.ts`. Registering `synthetic-shared-prefix` and `synthetic-shared-prefix-long-sensitive-suffix`, then delivering the longer value in chunks split after the shorter value, returned stdout `[redacted]-long-sensitive-suffix`. Subsequent redaction cannot recognize the exposed suffix.
findings.failure_scenario: Two registered credentials share a prefix, and a subprocess chunk ends at the shorter credential while printing the longer one.

gold.summary: Unlimited quota still applies utilization reserves to free and metered providers.

findings.title: Honor unlimited quota independently of billing type
findings.detail: Config accepts unlimited for every billing type, but headroom ignores windows only for subscription providers. Free and metered providers can display “No limit (configured)” while their observed windows make them unavailable. Reproduction command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-HPtVEX/claude-501 bun -e 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { Store } from "./src/db/store.ts"; import { ProviderTracker } from "./src/router/providers.ts"; const store = new Store(":memory:"); const t = new ProviderTracker([{id:"work",label:"Work",harness:"codex",billing:"free",quota:"unlimited",maxConcurrent:1}],store,{claudeFiveHour:0.8,claudeSevenDay:0.85,codexWeekly:0.9,codexFiveHour:0.9},{}); t.obse
findings.failure_scenario: Configure a free or metered Codex provider with quota="unlimited", then observe a five_hour window at 99% utilization. headroom becomes negative and isAvailable returns false despite the configured unlimited state.

findings.title: Unlimited quota still gates non-subscription providers
findings.detail: The request says an unlimited provider “always has headroom 1, and reserves don't gate it,” without restricting billing type. Config loading accepts unlimited with free or metered billing, but this guard bypasses windows only for subscriptions. Reproduction command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-nr9BPK/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-nr9BPK/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-nr9BPK/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-nr9BPK/claude-501/quota-review.ts`. Output: `free unlimited: {"headroom":-0.23749999999999993,"reason":"at reserve limit"}`. Consequently unavailableReason rejects the provider and routing excludes it.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure a Claude preset with billing = "free" and quota = "unlimited", then observe a five_hour window at 99%. The provider becomes unavailable at its reserve limit.

findings.title: Persisted window alerts survive switching to unlimited
findings.detail: The request says observed windows are “for information only” and “Quota alerts don't fire for an unlimited provider's windows.” The new observation guard prevents creating alerts, but startup refresh retains existing persisted window alerts. The API returns these alerts and Dashboard renders them. Reproduction command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-nr9BPK/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-nr9BPK/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-nr9BPK/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-nr9BPK/claude-501/quota-review.ts`. After closing and reopening SQLite with unlimited configured, output was `alerts after unlimited restart: [{"provider":"claude","window":"five_hour","utilization":0.99,"resetsAt":null,"severity":"exhauste
findings.failure_scenario: A windows-mode provider records a 99% window with no known reset, creating an exhausted alert. Configure unlimited and restart. The alert remains visible indefinitely, even after another observation.

gold.summary: A fixed review-time cutoff excludes worktrees created before the sidecar-writing release actually started.

findings.title: Use installation provenance instead of a fixed commit timestamp
findings.detail: The commit timestamp does not establish when an installation began running the sidecar-writing release. An installation can continue running the previous release after this cutoff, creating legitimate worktrees that this migration excludes. Those runs skip registration and still fail with Missing trusted Git paths. A targeted check using bun -e with an in-memory bun:sqlite database, a successful prepare at 1791185704000, and this migration failed with: AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: null !== 'legacy'. A separate Store upgrade reproduction printed: Old release prepared worktree after commit cutoff; eligible for registration: false.
findings.failure_scenario: An installation stays on the pre-#323 release until October 5, creates and parks a run that day, then upgrades. Its successful prepare is later than October 4's commit timestamp, so provenance remains null and resuming fails without recording the legacy worktree.

findings.title: Include legacy worktrees interrupted before the first gate
findings.detail: The clause “When a run resumes and its worktree is a linked worktree with no record, record it once” also covers interruption during prepare after worktree creation. This migration excludes that run unless prepare succeeded or emitted a gate event. On resume, engine.ts skips registration and headSha fails with Missing trusted Git paths. A targeted migration reproduction returned worktree_provenance: null for a pre-upgrade cancelled prepare without gate events. Exact command: bun -e 'import {Database} from "bun:sqlite"; const d=new Database(":memory:"); d.exec("CREATE TABLE runs(id); INSERT INTO runs VALUES (1); CREATE TABLE stages(run_id,name,started_at,finished_at,status); INSERT INTO stage
findings.failure_scenario: The previous release creates a linked worktree, then shuts down during prepare before any gate event. After upgrade, migration leaves provenance null; resume skips registration and fails on its first Git call.

findings.title: Register source-owned legacy local worktrees
findings.detail: The clause “When a run resumes and its worktree is a linked worktree with no record, record it once” includes legacy local worktrees owned by the source repository. This call always supplies cachePath, while recordLegacyWorktree only discovers administration in that bare cache. The existing alternate path is documented and exercised by test/pipeline.test.ts:790, which explicitly verifies that the cache does not exist. A temporary source-owned linked-worktree reproduction returned “Unsafe worktree Git administration”, left the sidecar absent, and its next headSha returned “Missing trusted Git paths”.
findings.failure_scenario: A local run created before factory-owned clones has a source-owned linked worktree without a sidecar and qualifies as legacy. Resume attempts registration against a nonexistent or unrelated factory cache and fails before continuing the run.

gold.summary: Rate-limit refusals leave rerun claims unresolved across cooldowns and restarts.
ANSI-colored Bun failures and pytest security failures are missed by the retry exclusion.

findings.title: Search intervening attempts when reconciling a rerun
findings.detail: Reconciliation only searches the workflow's latest attempt. A job-specific rerun does not include unrelated jobs, so a subsequent rerun of another job makes the originating result unreachable. The classifier throws 'Ambiguous CI rerun job' and leaves the ledger pending indefinitely. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review-repro.test.ts". Output: Expected: "failed_then_passed"; Received: "rerunning"; error: "Error: Ambiguous CI rerun job".
findings.failure_scenario: Job A fails in attempt 1 and passes in attempt 2 at the same SHA. Before the next poll, job B is rerun in attempt 3. Attempt 3 contains only B, so A's successful rerun is never recorded.

findings.title: Isolate CI inspection errors to the affected PR
findings.detail: A classification exception escapes record() and aborts observation of all remaining PRs in the repository. Because the failed inspection remains pending, a persistent failure repeats this starvation every poll. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review-repro.test.ts". Output: Expected to contain: "https://github.com/o/r/pull/2"; Received: ["https://github.com/o/r/pull/1", "https://github.com/o/r/pull/1"]. Logs repeatedly report 'Incomplete CI inspection: actions/jobs/21/logs (404)'.
findings.failure_scenario: The first tracked PR has a failed Actions job whose logs were deleted or expired and return 404. Every poll aborts before saving observations for subsequent PRs, suppressing their CI, review, and merge updates.

findings.title: Persisted main-red pauses bypass the GraphQL-change guard
findings.detail: The request says: “Fetch the failing check runs and jobs by REST, only when the GraphQL state changed.” A main-red pause persists ciPending=true, which re-enters classifyCi on unchanged observations and fetches the failing PR checks again. Command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-nHrYHx/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-nHrYHx/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-nHrYHx/claude-501 bun test /private/tmp/lr-nHrYHx/claude-501/ci-entry-review.test.ts. findings.title: Collision handling hardcodes the single id 'claude/haiku-5.5' instead of a general rule
findings.detail: The startup loop special-cases `existing.id === "claude/haiku-5.5"`. Any other runtime entry that later duplicates a newly added built-in still throws `catalog collision` and crashes the daemon at startup. That is exactly the failure this step was meant to prevent, and it will recur with the next built-in model. A model id hardcoded in Factory wiring is also out of keeping with the rest of the catalog code.

findings.title: Startup can still fail when operator routing names an effort the built-in doesn't support
findings.detail: After the built-in replaces the runtime entry, RuntimePolicy's constructor validates stored operator routing cells against the built-in's supportedEfforts (low/medium/high). If the runtime entry declared other efforts (e.g. none or xhigh), and an operator cell or pinned run uses them, validatePolicy throws and Factory construction fails. I confirmed that validatePolicy rejects `claude/haiku-5.5@xhigh` and `@none` with 'Unsupported effort ... supported: low, medium, high'. This contradicts the requirement that startup must not fail.

After upgrade, `new Factory()` throws `triage.small: ... Unsupported effort "none" for claude/haiku-5.5` and the daemon will not start.

findings.title: Retrying a pre-change run whose chain pins the removed model fails
findings.detail: Requirement 4 says records written before the change must render and resume. Stored routing cells and preferences are now filtered generically, but retryRun passes the inherited run.models through createRun -> validateRunModels. That validator still rejects unknown model ids, so a run that pinned the machine-named model (or any removed id) cannot be retried. The retryRun comment already says inherited chains 'predate this constraint', and they could be filtered with filterRetiredTargets the same way persisted operator cells are.

findings.title: `limitless local` throws on an IPv6 remote_host
findings.detail: manageLocal builds `new URL(`http://${host}:8080`)` without brackets. For a bare IPv6 literal (e.g. remote_host = "fe80::1"), URL construction throws a TypeError. That aborts the whole command, including the oMLX report that is already computed. The old code never parsed the host.

findings.title: MCP/digest privacy filter now withholds any text that contains the literal "[redacted]"
findings.detail: loadOutputPrivacy now returns "[withheld: private text]" for any string containing "[redacted]". The request did not ask for this, and no added test covers it. Gate output, land reasons and errors now normally carry the redaction marker after this change, so explainStatus (mcp-status.ts) and the digest (digest.ts) blank out whole fields instead of showing the redacted text. The same happens to any run title or prompt that just mentions "[redacted]" (e.g. an issue about redaction like this one). That loses information in an unrelated subsystem.

findings.title: FailureExcerpts lost its per-line cap and re-redacts the whole window on every line (≈19x slower)
findings.detail: The old code capped each retained line at 8,000 chars and used a simple shift. The new code keeps lines at full length. Once the window is full, every further diagnostic line triggers join + redactCredentials + split over ~40 lines, and each line is already redacted twice before that (in run.ts observe and again in observe()). All of this runs synchronously in the line callbacks on the factory's event loop, and retained lines are no longer bounded in memory.

findings.title: Truncation overlap ignores the longer JSON-escaped credential variants
findings.detail: redactGateStreams drops `secret.length - 1` chars after a runner cut. But registerCredential now also redacts JSON-escaped variants, which can be longer, e.g. a secret with newlines or quotes. If the cut lands inside an escaped variant, a suffix longer than the overlap can survive.
